first.rationale: The two measured declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly linked, with onboarding friction upstream of activation. memory_86 and memory_31 both point at friction reduction as the lever with durable rather than borrowed gains, so I want the original records for exactly those two: memory_86 to confirm the completion lift persisted past the first week and was not just funnel reshuffling, and memory_31 to see which fields were cut and whether the 'durable' claim was measured beyond first-week activation. I am deliberately not spending budget on memory_73: promotional_pricing is the obvious reflex against a competitor's entry pricing, but the memory already carries its own explicit warning that it materially damaged 30-day retention and should not be generalized. Matching a price attack would buy acquisition against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so the competitor move is best treated as pressure to fix our own funnel rather than as a reason to discount. Downstream value risk is real and is the main thing that could make this backfire: cutting required signup fields removes the firmographic data that routes and qualifies leads, and memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted demo path. A blanket field cut could raise raw activation while quietly degrading qualified pipeline, which would look like a win on the dashboard and a loss on revenue. So the experiment should be scoped to the self-serve SMB path only, leave the enterprise demo-request flow untouched, and instrument qualified-pipeline and 30-day retention as guardrail metrics alongside completion. Uncertainty I am holding open: the inherited memories are aggregate summaries with no visible confidence intervals or segment breakdowns, the day-52 and day-12 results predate the current competitive environment, and I cannot yet rule out that the activation drop is composition-driven (worse-fit accounts arriving because of the competitor) rather than friction-driven. If verification shows memory_86's lift was short-horizon only, I would switch to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger decline and carries less lead-data risk.
